beats.story: There's only half an hour until the meeting starts. Every muscle in my body is tense, my bones so heavy I feel as if I could fall through my chair. I take a deep breath and square my shoulders. If I'm going to do this, I need to get into that meeting room now. But just as I'm about to lift myself up, Caitlin huffs and bangs out of her chair, grabbing her phone and barreling back toward the boardroom. "Don't go in there!" Rhonda calls right when Caitlin reaches the threshold. "I'm just going to sit for a while," Caitlin says, sighing. "I need a break." There's something off about her -- she sounds worn, her lips thin and chin bent low.
beats.story_cn: 距离会议开始只剩半小时。我浑身每一块肌肉都绷得发紧，骨头沉得仿佛要坐穿椅子。深吸一口气，我挺直肩背——既然必须面对，此刻就该走进会议室。可就在我即将起身时，凯特琳猛地从椅子上弹起来，抓着手机径直冲向会议室门口。“别进去！”罗达的喊声在门槛处截住她。“就进去坐坐，”凯特琳叹着气说，“我需要喘口气。”她状态有些不对——声音疲惫，嘴唇抿得极薄，下巴深深垂着。

beats.story: Rhonda shakes her head, her hanging earrings jangling. "Not in there. Gregory's got a meeting soon and I need to set the waters up." Fucking hell. I forgot that Gregory has Rhonda treat his meetings like he's the CEO on Mad Men. She'd be only too happy to wheel in a whiskey cart if the custom still applied. Caitlin sighs again and pauses for a second like she's debating her response. "Whatever," she finally says, and returns to her desk, stuffing her phone back into her five-hundred-dollar basic black purse. I know the cost only because when Kyle gifted it to her for their anniversary, Garret held it up and announced it to the whole room.
beats.story_cn: 罗达摇着头，垂坠的耳环叮当作响。“别进那儿。格雷戈瑞马上要开会，我得去布置茶水区。”见鬼。我忘了格雷戈瑞总让罗达把会议安排得像《广告狂人》里总裁出巡，若按老派规矩她准乐意推着威士忌推车进去。凯特琳又叹了口气，停顿片刻似乎在斟酌回应。“随便吧，”她最终说道，转身回工位，将手机塞进那只五万块的基础款黑皮包。我之所以知道价格，是因为去年凯尔送她当周年礼物时，加瑞特当场举起来向全办公室公布了价码。

beats.story: I need to get in there. But with Rhonda keeping watch, I've got no chance. And judging from the fresh steaming cup of tea on her desk and the Excel grid I can see open on her computer, mouse hovering on the first row, she's there for the long haul. I need to distract everyone, and fast. And I know only one thing that is guaranteed to get everyone up from their desks in a matter of seconds. Before I can think too hard, I'm out of my chair. I head toward the bathroom, then pivot and speed walk down the hallway to the elevator. As soon as the doors open to the lobby, I race toward Artistic Coffee, the café next to our building.
beats.story_cn: 我必须进去。但罗达守着门，毫无机会。看她桌上新沏的热茶、电脑里打开的Excel表格，光标停在第一行——她显然要打持久战。我得立刻引开所有人，而且只知道一个百分百能让人瞬间离席的妙招。没等细想，我已经弹离座位。假意走向洗手间，转身疾步冲向电梯。门刚开进大堂，我便朝着我们楼旁的“艺术咖啡”狂奔而去。

beats.story: One only makes a purchase here out of desperation. The "artistry" from its namesake must be performative: keeping a straight face while serving diarrhea juice. Mara, the alleged barista who has been working here since I started, doesn't acknowledge me as I walk in. I move up to the counter and call, "Are your scones your cheapest pastries?" She nods, finally turning to look directly at me. Several piercings rise with her brows as she eyes me up. "Great, I'll take three please." The clock is ticking. Three forty-seven p.m. She bags them up and hands them to me with her heavily ringed fingers.
beats.story_cn: 只有走投无路之人才会来此消费。那位"艺术大师"的创作想必也是场行为艺术——面不改色地端出腹泻汁。那个自称咖啡师的玛拉，自我入职起就在此工作，此刻我进门时眼皮都没抬。我走到柜台前喊道："你们的司康是点心里最便宜的吗？"她点点头，终于转过脸正眼看我。眉毛挑起时几枚穿刺饰品也随之抬动，她上下打量着我。"很好，请给我拿三个。"时间分秒流逝。下午三点四十七分。她将司康装袋，戴着满手夸张戒指的手指递来纸袋。

beats.story: The scones are hard as rocks and probably dry as shit, but that's for the best. This can't be too flashy; anything too good, like Cliff's donuts, and the entire floor would be up in an instant, marking me as the outlier. I make my way back up to the office and swipe myself into the big lunchroom. Luckily, it's completely empty, the lights off. I drop the scones onto the center of the table and head back to the pods. Armin is drooping so low in his chair it's a wonder he doesn't fall face- first onto his desk. Caitlin is slowly clacking away. Rhonda is taking a sip from her mug, humming to herself as she moves her icon from row 2 to row 3 of her grid.
beats.story_cn: 司康坚如磐石且干如沙砾，但这恰到好处。不能太过惹眼；若是像克里夫的甜甜圈那样美味，整层楼的人都会瞬间涌来，将我标记为异类。我溜回办公室，刷卡进入大休息室。幸运的是空无一人，灯火未熄。我把司康扔到长桌中央，转身返回格子间。阿尔敏瘫在椅子里低垂着脑袋，简直要脸朝下栽进办公桌。凯特琳正缓慢地噼啪打字。朗达端着马克杯抿了口咖啡，哼着小曲将光标从表格第二行挪到第三行。

beats.story: How to get them up without alerting the entire office? I sit down at my desk and go into my email, clicking open a blank message. My mouse hovers over my name to the option beneath it in the "From" section. I've used the admin account only to read other people's emails, not compose one of my own. I suck in air through my teeth and summon my most admin of admin voices: From: Supershops Admin BCC: Caitlin Joffrey; Armin Habib; Rhonda Staples Subject: Thank you for your great work Dear Supershops employee, To express our appreciation to our most hardworking employees this quarter, we've sent special gifts to lunchroom number 417. Please collect your own gift ASAP. One per person. Regards, Management I hit send, and it's instantaneous.
beats.story_cn: 怎样才能把他们引上去而不惊动全办公室？我坐回工位打开邮箱，点开新邮件。鼠标悬停在"发件人"栏我的名字上，移向下方选项。我用管理员账号只读过他人邮件，从未亲自撰文。我牙缝里嘶嘶吸着气，调动出最刻板的行政腔调：发件人：超级商店管理员 收件人（密送）：凯特琳·乔弗里；阿尔敏·哈比布；朗达·斯塔普尔斯 主题：感谢你们卓越的付出 亲爱的超级商店同仁： 为表彰本季度最勤勉的员工，特向417号休息室赠送专属礼品。请即刻领取。每人一份。管理部敬上 点击发送的瞬间，指令即刻生效。

beats.story: Before I can even indulge in my dread, I hear the distinctive double tap of Rhonda opening her email. My heart is attempting to break from my rib cage and sprint across the office. After a beat, Rhonda shrugs and stands up, heading toward the lunchroom. A few seconds later Caitlin gets up too. I'm somehow both relieved and scared shitless. Armin doesn't go, but the good news is he might actually be dead with the way his lifeless body is leaning on the desk. This is my chance. Through my pounding heart and dry throat, I make my way into the boardroom.
beats.story_cn: 我还没来得及沉溺在恐惧中，就听见朗达点开邮件时特有的两声轻敲。我的心脏正试图挣脱肋骨的囚笼，横穿整个办公室去狂奔。停顿片刻后，朗达耸耸肩起身，朝茶水间走去。几秒钟后凯特琳也站了起来。我莫名同时感到释然与恐惧。阿尔敏没动，不过好消息是，他那瘫在桌上的死气沉沉的模样，可能真的已经“去世”了。就是现在。穿过狂跳的心脏和发干的喉咙，我朝会议室走去。

beats.story: Panic closes in while I'm scanning for a spot to leave the phone. It's too barren to hide anything well. I rush to my desk, pull the tissue box from my bottom drawer, drop my phone in, and sprint back to the boardroom to leave it on the table. I'll have to hope nobody has any cold symptoms. I emerge just as Larry Goodwin passes. I stop in my tracks in the threshold like a deer in headlights as he walks around me. A half second later, Gregory exits his office. I'm going to shit my pants.
beats.story_cn: 恐慌在搜寻藏手机的地方时汹涌逼近。这里太空旷，什么都没法藏好。我冲回工位，从底层抽屉抽出纸巾盒，把手机塞进去，又奔回会议室搁在桌上。只能祈祷没人感冒了。刚出来就撞见拉里·古德温经过。当他从我身边绕过时，我僵在门槛上像只车灯前的鹿。半秒后，格雷戈里从办公室出来了。我吓得要当场失禁。

beats.story: I put on my best neutral face and trot back to my desk. Just as I sit down, Caitlin and Rhonda round the corner, a scone each in hand. Caitlin smiles and says way too loud, "It's so nice to have our hard work recognized." Larry Goodwin halts in his tracks, dripping a slosh of water from his freshly filled bottle. "You guys got praised? What for?" Caitlin speaks louder, chin jutting out. "Oh, just some of us got a little something in recognition of our hard work. It was in an email." Her eyes tilt my way as Larry's narrow on the scone in her hand. Armin jostles awake, squinty-eyed.

beats.story: So I wait another fifteen minutes in agony. Finally, once I'm certain that everyone is thoroughly entranced by the light of their monitors, I head to the boardroom. When I step back out, I halt when I clock Armin watching me. His eyes shift, before he turns back to his monitor and throws his earphones back over his head. I stand there for a beat, clutching my phone. There's no way he noticed I didn't walk in with it. I'm sure I'm just being paranoid.
beats.story_cn: 于是我在煎熬中又等待了十五分钟。终于确认所有人都沉溺于屏幕荧光后，我走向会议室。退出时瞥见阿明正盯着我，立即刹住脚步。他的眼神游移片刻，随即转身戴上耳机。我攥着手机僵立一瞬——他不可能发现我空手进来的。一定是我想太多了。

options.action: Take a calculated initiative to respond gracefully to unprecedented workplace encounters.
options.action_cn: 审时度势，主动出击，优雅应对职场突发状况。
options.fullOutcomeStory: Jolene kept her head clear and chose to respond gracefully to unprecedented workplace encounters. Her sharp wit and cautious maneuvering allowed her to navigate the tense moment without blowing her cover.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 茱莉兰保持头脑清醒，选择优雅应对职场突发状况。她机敏的才智与谨慎的穿针引线，助她安然度过紧张时刻而不露破绽。

options.action: Hesitate nervously and show signs of second-guessing yourself.
options.action_cn: 紧张迟疑，反复掂量。
options.fullOutcomeStory: A momentary lapse in confidence caused everyone to stare in awkward silence. Caitlin seized the opportunity to throw a sarcastic smirk across the room.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 一时信心溃散引得众人尴尬侧目。凯特琳趁机朝房间那头投去一抹嘲讽的笑意。

options.action: Overreact impulsively and blurt out something awkward.
options.action_cn: 冲动过激，脱口而出尴尬场面。
options.fullOutcomeStory: An impulsive burst of stress led to a bizarre remark that echoed through the quiet office. You immediately regretted speaking without filtering.
options.fullOutcomeStory_cn: 压力迸发的失言在寂静办公室里荡开回声。你立刻懊悔未加过滤便开了口。
